raw_text:
[[PW0:001]]
Today I was fixing a problem where remote WeChat does not display images.
[[PW0:002]]
I initially suspected causes across dimensions like the WeChat database, kernel dirty pages, IO load, CDN, Clash, and so on.
[[PW0:003]]
But I am in the middle of porting DeepSeek 4.1, and several other projects are being designed, so I am too busy.
[[PW0:004]]
I directly handed the environment and Docker services to the AI, letting it only probe and analyze, strictly forbidding it from touching the environment or source code. Five minutes later, the AI said the Clash tool had a problem — it was incorrectly redirecting Tencent's image CDN to the proxy, so all images took a detour through the United States, which is why images could not be seen and sending images was slow.
[[PW0:005]]
The AI boss is still impressive; as long as you give it enough environment, it can run all kinds of A/B tests and automatically analyze and troubleshoot issues. Someone like me, a Linux system engineer with many years of experience, can only shine the AI boss's shoes.
[[PW0:006]]
No, I am not even worthy of shining shoes.
[[PW0:END]]
